intro: Framework for the weekly stale listings hour. Redfin defines a stale listing as 60+ days without a contract. Our tiers: Watch (1 to 29 days), Stale (30 to 59), Ultra Stale (60 to 89), Extremely Stale (90+).

moves.label: Price adjustment (one decisive move)
moves.desc: One 3 to 7% adjustment (7 to 10% past 45 days) framed as a second launch. Replace multiple small cuts with one that re-ranks the home.

moves.label: Reposition on a search bracket
moves.desc: Price so the home appears in the next buyer search band: just under the band below $1M ($999K), on the round number at $1M+ so both filters catch it.

moves.label: Thursday drop
moves.desc: Post the adjustment Wednesday night or Thursday to hit hot sheets and weekend tour planning. Pair it with new lead photo and copy.

moves.label: Rocket 2-1 buydown offer
moves.desc: Seller-funded temporary buydown advertised in remarks with the year-1 monthly savings. Costs about 2.3% of the loan and cuts the buyer's payment far more than the same dollars as a price cut.

moves.label: Permanent rate buydown
moves.desc: Seller-paid points (about 1% of loan per 0.25% rate) marketed as a lower lifetime payment through Rocket.

moves.label: Closing-cost credit
moves.desc: Fixed-dollar credit stated in remarks within loan-type caps (conventional 3 to 9%, FHA 6%). Concessions appear in 54.8% of LA sales already.

moves.label: Photo refresh
moves.desc: Reshoot or re-edit to 25+ pro photos. Strongest exterior leads, best five features in the first five frames, cut dark or vertical shots.

moves.label: Twilight, floor plan, 3D and video
moves.desc: Add a twilight hero, floor plan and 3D tour (Zillow: 3D-tour listings sell 14% faster) plus a 60 second walkthrough.

moves.label: Remarks rewrite
moves.desc: Lead with the top three features from showing feedback and buyer search keywords (garage, walk-in closet, family room). State the incentive. Remove distress words like motivated or won't last.

moves.label: Staging reset
moves.desc: Stage living room, primary bedroom and kitchen, or declutter and neutralize. 49% of listing agents report less time on market with staging.

moves.label: Pre-inspection and repairs
moves.desc: Order a pre-listing inspection, fix the recurring feedback items, publish the report to cut fall-through risk before any relaunch.

moves.label: Access unlock
moves.desc: Remove notice requirements, add a lockbox or instant confirm, widen windows. Buyer agents drop hard-to-show homes from tours.

moves.label: Relaunch open house
moves.desc: Public open house at the new price inviting prior showings, neighbors and the database; back-to-back weekend opens.

moves.label: Broker open and showing-agent callbacks
moves.desc: Agent-only preview to collect written pricing and condition feedback; call every agent who showed and every agent on nearby pendings.

moves.label: Reverse prospecting and reverse offer
moves.desc: Query CRMLS saved searches that match the new price and send the listing directly; send written terms to anyone who toured twice or lowballed.

moves.label: Paid social and email push
moves.desc: Targeted ads to the price band and feeder zips; feature in the weekly buyer email and Nextdoor.

moves.label: Weekly written seller report
moves.desc: Showings, feedback, inquiries, open house results, new comps and Redfin traffic every week so the data makes the ask, not the agent.

moves.label: Withdraw and relist (30-day reset)
moves.desc: Written seller instruction, off CRMLS 30+ days (CDAM resets after 30 days off-MLS since Nov 2025), fix something material, relist under a new number. Disclose cumulative DOM honestly.

moves.label: Cost-of-waiting seller meeting
moves.desc: Face to face with carrying cost plus the discount curve versus a one-time adjustment. Offer three paths and get a decision.

moves.label: Expectation reset and exit plan
moves.desc: Address the expiration date; document the seller's decision; set an extension or cancellation path.

moves.label: No change (with reason)
moves.desc: Document why the listing stays as is and the date it will be reviewed again.

diagnostics.signals: Views fine but favorites low; showings but no offers; feedback says nice but high; list above Redfin Estimate; comps closing lower since launch; no Hot Home badge.
diagnostics.fix: 10-10-0 rule: 10 days with 0 showings or 10 showings with 0 offers means price. One decisive adjustment, not a series.

diagnostics.signals: Feedback repeats the same defect; offers arrive with heavy repair credits or fall out at inspection.
diagnostics.fix: If two or more agents cite the same defect it is condition, not price. Pre-inspection, fix, publish.

diagnostics.signals: Day-1 views weak versus similar new listings; under 25 photos; no twilight, floor plan or 3D; dark or phone photos.
diagnostics.fix: Reshoot to 25+ (Zillow average is 33). 81% of buyers rate photos the most useful online feature.

diagnostics.signals: Generic bed and bath copy; no search keywords; mentions of prior price or motivated seller.
diagnostics.fix: Rewrite around the three features buyers cite; name the incentive; end with a call to action.

diagnostics.signals: 24-hour notice, appointment only, tenant occupied, no lockbox; showing requests declined or rescheduled.
diagnostics.fix: Treat any restriction as a cause until removed.

diagnostics.signals: No open house; no boost; no outreach to prior showings; no reverse prospecting.
diagnostics.fix: Weekly report, open houses, seasonal photos, database alert, social, door knock before any price ask.

diagnostics.signals: No weekly written update; no showing feedback log; no refreshed CMA.
diagnostics.fix: Every 21 days the market renews: meet the seller with an updated CMA.

diagnostics.signals: Rejects showings, refuses concessions, anchors on a 2022 neighbor sale, waiting for spring.
diagnostics.fix: Pre-frame the review cadence at listing; document refusals; set an exit plan.

watch.title: Watch: 1 to 29 days
watch.goal: Protect the launch window. Views fall 50% on day 2 and are at 17% of day 1 by day 30.
steps: Confirm 25+ photos, twilight hero, floor plan, open house weekend one.
Set the pre-listing pact with the seller: fewer than 5 showings by day 14 or 10 showings and no offers by day 21 triggers a pricing review.
Log Redfin views and favorites weekly from day 1 so the decay curve is visible.
Call every showing agent within 24 hours.
rules: No Hot Home badge by day 10 with normal traffic: check price against the Redfin Estimate.
Under 5 showings by day 14: exposure or access problem first, then price.

stale.title: Stale: 30 to 59 days (drifting)
stale.goal: Separate exposure problems from price problems and make one decisive move before day 60.
steps: Run the diagnostic: showings per week, showing-to-offer ratio, views versus day 1, favorites, Estimate gap, newer competition.
Fix non-price causes first so the price ask is credible: access, lead photo, remarks, floor plan.
Call every agent who showed and the agents on nearby pendings to learn what buyers chose instead.
Broker open plus public open house as a feedback event.
Decision at day 30 to 45: 10+ showings and 0 offers, or under 1 showing a week, means one 3 to 7% adjustment posted Wednesday night.
rules: Views below 17% of day 1 with no offers: exposure first, re-measure at day 45.
Views at or above benchmark with no offers: price.
LA median DOM is 49, so 30 to 59 days is near median but the attention is gone.

ultra.title: Ultra Stale: 60 to 89 days (Redfin's stale line)
ultra.goal: Second launch, not a number change.
steps: Rerun the CMA on everything listed, pending, sold and expired since launch.
Reprice to where the home is dramatically more competitive: 7 to 10% past 45 days; LA sellers who cut averaged 7.0% in Feb 2026.
Refresh lead photo, reorder gallery, rewrite remarks, new social content, second open house inviting prior showings and neighbors.
Add a financing play: seller-paid 2-1 buydown or closing credit, written into remarks with the monthly savings.
Reverse offer to any buyer who toured twice or lowballed; reverse prospect CRMLS saved searches at the new price.
Decision at day 75: no offers after reduction and relaunch means schedule the day-90 withdraw and relist conversation now.
rules: One cut looks strategic; several small cuts look desperate. Maximum two: one decisive, one relaunch.
A cut must cross a search band or it is invisible.
No Hot Home badge after the reduction means the reduction was not big enough to change the model's view.

extreme.title: Extremely Stale: 90+ days (chronic)
extreme.goal: Full reset with the seller: new price band, new condition, new media, or a pause.
steps: Seller reset meeting with cost-of-waiting math and the discount curve (2 to 2.5% more buyer discount per 30 days through six months, then 3.5 to 5%).
Offer three paths: reprice to the band where the home wins (often 5 to 10%+), withdraw 30+ days and fix condition, staging and photos before relisting, or pause and lease.
Pre-listing inspection and repairs before any relist.
Relist only when something material changed: price band, condition, media or terms.
Seller declines all three: document in writing and set an expiration or cancellation plan.
rules: Redfin shows a relist as new to buyers but LA buyer agents routinely pull CRMLS history. Never imply new to market.
Cumulative DOM resets only after 30 days off MLS (CRMLS, effective Nov 19 2025).
Many sellers withdraw around six months; get ahead of that date.

pricing: Trigger: 10 days with 0 showings or 10 showings with 0 offers (Byron Lazine's 10-10-0). National average to contract is about 8 showings; target 2 a week.

Size: 1 to 2% flies under the radar. 3 to 5% is the typical meaningful move; 3 to 7% standard, 7 to 10% when past 45 days. Redfin Feb 2026: sellers who cut averaged 7.3% nationally, 7.0% ($117,727) in LA, 6.0% in Anaheim, 6.4% in Riverside.

Cross a search band: $1,000,000 shows to buyers filtering up to $1M and from $1M; $999,000 is invisible to the second group. Under $1M use charm pricing just below the band; at round million marks price on the band.
Timing: Thursday is the modal day for cuts (18.5%). Post Wednesday night to hit Thursday hot sheets and weekend tours. A cut gives one day of lift (views 29 vs 17 indexed) so pair it with a relaunch.
How many: about 11% of US actives have three or more cuts. Coach to a maximum of two. Small cuts over 90 days net lower final prices than one meaningful reduction.
Chasing the market: overpricing by 10%+ adds more than a month of market time. The home is not competitive until the last price change, so price to where it wins today.
Language: price adjustment or price improvement, never cut, slash or reduce. Priced on the higher side, never overpriced.
Redfin Estimate: median on-market error is 1.89%. A list price more than 3 to 5% above the Estimate is a visible flag to buyers.
relaunch: CRMLS Cumulative Days Active (CDAM) resets after a property has been off the MLS for 30 days (effective Nov 19 2025; previously 90). Ownership transfer resets to zero.
Hold: valid contract, pause up to 30 days (renewable), DOM does not accrue, marketing allowed but no showings, requires the seller's written instruction.
Withdrawn: valid contract, no marketing or showings, DOM does not accrue; on reactivation DOM resumes from the withdrawal date.
Only a broker or office manager can move a listing to Canceled, and Canceled cannot be reverted.

Buyers see a DOM reset on Redfin after relist; agents see cumulative history and LA buyer agents routinely pull it. Articles 1 and 12 require truthful communication: never state or imply new to market, answer cumulative DOM questions honestly.

Relaunch checklist: seller written instruction, Withdrawn or Canceled, 30+ days off MLS, new photos, remarks, price band and terms, relist under a new number, notify prior showing agents and reverse prospect on day one, open house weekend one.
Redfin's alternative: phased marketing (Coming Soon or Private Exclusive) to test price before public DOM starts.

photoRubric.standard: Pro photos sell for more and about 21 fewer days (Redfin via Matterport)
Best five features in the first five photos; outdoor spaces not buried
3D-tour listings sell 14% faster and are 22% more likely to sell within 30 days (Zillow)
77% of buyers say a dynamic floor plan helps
Branded walkthrough; Showcase-style listings net about 2% more
Lead with searched features: garage, walk-in closet, family room; value-add finishes
Incentives stated explicitly with the dollar and monthly effect; easy showing instructions

scripts.title: Tom Ferry: alignment
scripts.text: Right now the agents in the market, the data, and the buyers are telling us the price isn't aligned. What would you like to do? I'm going to strongly recommend we amend the price to be in alignment with what buyers are willing to pay. For 90 days, buyers have compared your home to other homes from $__ to $__ and didn't like your home enough to make an offer.

scripts.title: Brian Buffini: the market renews
scripts.text: Every 21 days the real estate market renews and readjusts itself. I've prepared an updated market analysis. When can we meet? The market is telling us we're priced a little on the high side. If we adjust the price downward, we'll be taking a major step in the right direction.

scripts.title: Byron Lazine: 10-10-0 call
scripts.text: As promised, quick update. We're at [X] days on market, [Y] total showings, and so far the market has given us no written reaction. When we listed, we agreed on the 10-10-0 rule. We're at that point now. My recommendation is that we adjust the price to [number] so we move from being shopped to being chosen.

scripts.title: Saad Jamil: showings prove marketing
scripts.text: Eleven showings show marketing works. Zero offers means buyers like the home but not at this price. Buyers watch days on market like we watch comps. Past day 30, they assume something's wrong. One decisive reduction stops the bleeding. Objection, wait until spring: spring brings more inventory and buyers who already saw your home at the current price.

scripts.title: Tim and Julie Harris: second launch
scripts.text: This is a second launch, not a price change. You contribute through price, I contribute through execution: new lead photo, new copy, new social, a second open house with every prior showing invited, and a written report every week.

scripts.title: Aaron Novello: six phrases
scripts.text: Fair market value. The marketplace is showing us. Through no fault of your own or mine, marketplace dynamics have changed. Price is a snapshot in time. My job is to help you, never to talk you into anything. Whatever you decide, I'll support you 100%.

scripts.title: Redfin voice
scripts.text: Fair or not, buyers judge a home by how many days it has been on the market. Nine times out of 10, homes are selling for under asking; sometimes the price is just too high and sellers pull the home after six months.

stats.stat: Listings stale (60+ days): 52.2% US, 44.1% LA, 34.0% Anaheim, 48.8% Riverside (Feb 2026)
Sellers who cut before closing: 34.2% US (avg 7.3%); LA 24.0% (7.0%, $117,727) (Feb 2026 closings)
Active listings with a price drop: 21.1% US, 16.5% LA metro, 19.5% Anaheim, 17.8% Riverside/SB (4 weeks to Sep 20 2026)
Orange County: 43% of active listings have cut price (Oct 5 2026)
Buyer discount grows about 2 to 2.5% per 30 days on market through six months, then 3.5% to 5% per 30 days
Listing views: day 2 = 50% of day 1, week 1 = 25%, day 30 = 17%; a price drop lifts to 29% for one day
Overpricing by 10%+ adds more than a month of market time
Concessions in 46.2% of US sales, 54.8% of LA sales, 62.3% San Diego (May 2026)
Thursday is the modal day for price cuts (18.5%); typical cut 2.6 to 3.8%
Staging: 49% of listing agents say it cut time on market; 29% say offers rose 1 to 10%
3D tours: sell 14% faster, 22% more likely to sell within 30 days
Hot Home badge: 80%+ chance of an accepted offer within 14 days, recomputed daily
Beverly Hills: homes priced within 3% of value closed in 29 days at 99.1%; homes needing a reduction averaged $342K below original list and 73 days
2-1 buydown on a $1M price (20% down, 6.5% note): seller cost about $18,200; buyer saves about $1,003/mo in year 1. The same $18,200 as a price cut saves the buyer about $92/mo.
CRMLS: cumulative days on market resets after 30 days off MLS (effective Nov 19 2025)

financing: Seller concession caps: conventional 3 to 9% depending on down payment, FHA up to 6%, VA flexible.

2-1 buydown: year 1 at rate minus 2, year 2 at rate minus 1. Seller cost equals the sum of the payment savings, about 2.3% of the loan. Market it with the dollar amount and the monthly effect: Seller will fund a 2-1 rate buydown with acceptable offer, approximately $X per month lower payment in year one.

Permanent buydown: 1 point (1% of loan) buys roughly 0.25% off the rate; break-even about five years. A 1% permanent buydown on a $500K home (about $19K) equals the monthly savings of a roughly $49K price cut.
Concessions do not fix a wrong search band. Buyers never see the listing. Fix the band first, then add the financing hook.
